full_judgment:
Ahmed Sohel, J: On an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the accused-petitioner, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceeding of Special Case No.09 of 2003, arising out of Sitakundu Police Station Case No.12, dated 15-7-2000 under section 406/409/420 and 109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, now pending before the Court of learned Sessions Judge, Chattogram, should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that on 15-7-2000, one Mobinul Islam, Inspector, Durnity Daman Bureau, Bank Branch, Dhaka as informant lodged the FIR, before the Sitakundu Police Station, Chattogram, alleging, inter-alia, that the accused No.1, Md Nurul Haq Chowdhury, Proprietor of M/s Nurul Haq and Brothers, imported a ship, named "MV City of ZUG" and later on opened 'Loan General Account' with the United Commercial Bank Limited, Khatungonj Branch, Chattogram. Subsequently, upon approval by the Head Office of the said Bank, 'Loan General Account' was converted into a CC (Pledge) Account against the said ship/broken scraps, which was kept in the 'Ship Breaking Yard' at Madambibir Hat, Sitakundu, Chattogram. Thereafter, the accused No.1 in connivance with the accused No. 2, Mr Abdul Khaleque, the then Manager of United Commercial Bank Limited, Khatungonj Branch, Chattogram, misappropriated the money of the Bank amounting to Taka 1,01,08,530, by selling out the .ship broken scraps without the delivery order of the said Bank. Hence, the FIR. 

 3. On the basis of the said FIR, Sitakundu Police Station Case No.12 dated 15-7-2000, under section 406/420/109 of the Penal Code read with 5(2) of the Prevention of Anti-Corruption Act, 1947 has been started against the accused-petitioner and others. 4. After investigation, the police sub-mitted charge-sheet being No. 44 dated 31-3-2003, under section 406/409/420/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption of Act, 1947, against the accused-petitioner and others. 

 5. Thereafter, the case record was transferred to the Special Tribunal, Chattogram for trial and the same was renumbered as Special Case No.9 of 2003. On 28-8-2003, the learned Senior Special Judge, Chattogram received the said case for trial. No cognizance has been taken till date, due to absconsion of the accused No.1, Nurul Haq Chowdhury. The accused-petitioner obtained ad-interim bail from the Hon'ble High Court Division of Supreme Court of Bangladesh in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7303 of 2003. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the proceeding of the Special Case No.09 of 2003, corresponding to GR Case No.111 of 2000, arising out of Sitakundu Police Station Case No.12 dated 15-7-2000, under section 406/409/420 and 109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, pending before the Court of Sessions Judge, Chattogram, the present accused-petitioner approached before this court with an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay of all further proceedings of the aforesaid case, so far it relates to the accused petitioner. Subsequently, the said stay has been extended from time to time. 

 8. He further submits that the accused-petitioner, was in-charge, of Advance Department and Vice President, United Commercial Bank Limited, Chattogram who has been implicated in the charge-sheet on the allegation of breach of trust but he is not a public servant and also other accuseds of this case are not public servants, under the provision of section 21 of the Bangladesh Penal Code. Therefore, the learned Senior Special Judge, Chattogram has no jurisdiction to proceed with the trial of the case. 

 9. He next submits that the Complainant-Bank, filed Artha Rin Suit No. 95 of 2005 against the accused No. 1, Md Nurul Haq Chowdhury and others, for realization of loan money which was subsequently decreed on 31-10-2011. However, having found no involvement of the accused-petitioner in the instant case, he has not been impleaded in the said Artha Rin Suit as defendant. Furthermore, the learned Advocate forcefully submits that the allegation against the petitioner is civil in nature and, as such, the criminal proceeding does not lie against him. Therefore, initiation and continuation of the proceeding is liable to be quashed for securing the ends of justice. Accordingly, he prays for making the Rule absolute. 

 10. On the other hand, Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the Anti-Corruption Commission, opposes the Rule and submits that all the issues raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, has already been settled by our Apex Court. He has pointed out that although petitioner is not the FIR named, however, charge-sheet discloses offence against the accused-petitioner. In the instant case, no cognizance has been taken yet, therefore, the application under 561A is a premature one and not maintainable in the eye of law as per the decision reported in the 60 DLR (AD) 1. 

 11. He next submits that the Investigating Officer in the charge-sheet clearly stated that the accused-petitioner, Sanjib Kumar Sen as in-charge of loan department of United Commercial Bank Limited, Khatungonj Branch, Chattogram helped the accused, No. 1 Md Nurul Haq Chowdhury, to embezzle the bank money and also the issue that the Bank officials are public servant, has already been settled by our Apex Court. Therefore, the contention of the petitioner that he is not involved with the said offence, is matter of evidence, which can be decided only at the time of trial. He further pointed out that there is no illegality to proceed with the criminal case, when the Complainant Bank has obtained decree in the Artha Rin Suit No. 95 of 2005, as because, criminal case stands for the offence, while civil suit is for realization of money. 

 12. He finally submits that the grounds taken and the arguments as advanced by the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner are all disputed question of facts, which can be decided by taking evidence at the time of trial. There is no scope for interference with the instant case by this Court, in exercise of its inherent power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Accordingly, he prays for discharging the Rule. 

 16. So, the question arises as to whether or not the impugned proceeding should be quashed. In order to decide this issue, we have to examine the extent of power, scope, and categories of cases in which High Court Division may invoke its power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In fact, the scope of this section is very narrow. 

 17. In the case of Abdul Quader Chowdhury vs the State, reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38, it has been clearly spelt out the categories of cases where the High Court Division should interfere under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the purpose of quashing a proceeding, one of the following conditions must be satisfied: 

 (1) Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on admitted facts no case stands against the accused. 

 (4) In a case where the allegations in the FIR or the petition of complaint, even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirely, do not constitute the offence as alleged; and 

 (5) The allegations against the accused although constitute an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge. 

 18. On the principles for quashing the proceedings, similar view was subsequently followed in the case of Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain and others, reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16. 

 19. Further, in the case of Sher Ali vs the State, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 67, it has been held that:- 

 22. Further, it appears that no cognizance has yet been taken in the instant case. On this point, the view of our Apex Court has been focused in the decision of Abdul Huque and others vs State reported in 60 DLR (AD) 1, which is as follows: "Before taking of cognizance of a case by the competent Court or tribunal, a proceedings cannot be said to be pending and accordingly, a proceeding cannot be quashed unless cognizance in respect of thereof has been taken and process issued". 

 24. Now, in respect to the issue that, whether the Bank officials are public servants or not. This issue has been settled by our Appellate Division in long line of decisions. It has been held in the case of International Finance Investment and Commerce Bank Limited vs Abdul Quayum and another reported in 4 BLC (AD) 255 that 'Bank officials are public servants'. 

 26. On this point, our Apex Court held in the case of Khandader Abul Bashar and other vs the State, reported in 63 DLR (AD) 79, that- 

 "There is no legal impediment to filing a criminal case even if a civil suit is pending on the selfsame allegation provided the ingredients of offence are present." 

 27. From the above analysis, we can come to a conclusion that the civil case and the criminal case from the same facts can stand simultaneously, if the ingredients of the offence are present. 

 28. In the above facts and circumstances of the case, in our view the grounds taken by the accused-petitioner in the application for quashment of the instant case as well as the submissions as advanced by him, during the course of hearing, are all disputed question of facts, which can only be decided by the trial Court by taking evidence at the time of trial. The accused-petitioner has adequate opportunity to take his defence in the trial of the case by agitating all those grounds. It is settled principle of law that there is no scope to determine those disputed question of facts by exercising the inherent power of this Court under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 34. The learned Judge of the concerned trial Court is hereby directed to dispose of the case as early as possible preferably within 12(twelve) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order.
